Papnoute names the far mountain, the last field crossed, the stripping away of what is familiar. Among us the vow is kept where the familiar has not been left behind at all.

The bar qyama and bat qyama, the sons and daughters of the covenant, take the vow and stay. Not one field crossed. They keep the fast and the watch in the same town where their own kin still live, sleep under roofs near the h

I will not settle it, and I will not turn Papnoute's confession into a boast on his behalf. He says the desert could not trust its eyes while the face in the doorway still stood there. That is honest, and I let it stand as his.

But we part from it. We do not believe clear sight requires losing that face. Simeon stood before the king with his own people watching, and it was that watching which hel

Papnoute's word answers a walk already completed - land given up, feet already moved. Ours answers a promise not yet finished being kept.

Qyama means a standing, a thing set up to stand. It is spoken first, before kin who heard it said, and it must be stood in again tomorrow, in the same house, among the same kin. No land given up - the bar qyama and bat qyama keep the very ground they were born
